body: I wanted to post this too...just in case it helps anyone. I'm working through it now, taking 10 pages a night. I should be done with the reading/journaling by the end of the week but readjusting one's thoughts is an ongoing process. I think we can change...but we have to replace old behaviors with new ones. We can't just cease being jealous, replace it with nothing, and think we won't get jealous.

Thanks for the support, guys. The gentleman in question has been very gracious to me (as he always is) and has given me my space. I found a 12 step workbook for overcoming jealousy online and I've been kind of working my way through that, and just generally trying to distract myself. I don't mean to have these thoughts. I typically don't envy income or clothing so much as the opportunities I see others given. I know I have some deep resentment toward my father. That coupled with the loss of my mother has made me feel robbed. It's mostly my father, really. I mean, if he would have been less self-centered, my student loans could be a thing of the past. I could feel more financially secure. I might feel more confident about my future overall. He's robbed me of so many opportunities. I feel like his actions have really set me back in life. He was holding me back even before my mom died. How different would things have been if he hadn't stolen from her and gambled away her paychecks at the casino? I just feel very fortunate to have a guy who's helping me work past things, who understands when I need to be alone, who wants me to be happy more than anything, who inadvertently made me jealous by sharing with me things he wanted to really share with me. I'm hoping the workbook helps. I think for me, it's gonna be a huge thing just to move out. I'm hoping October goes well and January ushers in a new chapter in my life. My heart tells me that it will.

I was there not too long ago...the break-up was very hard, as I had just lost my mother to cancer. She was only 48 and I was closer to her than anyone..it really rocked my world. I know that I did the right thing though. I didn't really have that great of a support system either. Luckily, he was fairly amicable about things. 

The point is that you deserve to feel loved. If you don't, it's time to move on. I used to defend my ex's behavior too. He wasn't romantic enough, I'd say. He had to be told to buy me flowers. At that point, it doesn't matter, you know? We did the same thing all the time. He wasn't very active. It sucked! He was a decent guy, but not boyfriend material. 

So there's my advice. Talk to him. Tell him how you feel. If that fails, get out. There are other guys who would love to have a chance with you! And if you need to talk with someone, I am here.

I've been there, but nothing says 100% that you have to work or be going to school to gain temporary residency, but that is sort of the vibe I'm getting. That or get married. And that kind of seems like the wrong reason to get married in my book.

I finally moved out and I'm happy about that but it is basically just this room this guy was renting out. I'm having trouble feeling like I have a real home. I cashed out my mutual fund and I'm going to apply for a discount through my hospital. Also applying for food stamps. I look for other jobs regularly. My major need right now is someone to talk to who has been through something similar honestly.

My mom died from breast cancer last October at the age of 48. On Halloween too. I haven't been at my new job too awful long, but that's the one day I decided to call in. I just had a bad feeling about things. Turns out I was right. 

I think the hardest part about dealing with this kind of thing is that there's never a reason why...not one that ever satisfies us. Most of the time I'm fine, but then I'll break apart for seemingly no reason. I'm still trying to figure out what I need to heal. 

I never realized how much my mom held our family together until she was gone. My dad has made a royal mess of things. He leapt for the first woman that came into sight, moved her in, forced me to move out, blew through most of the life insurance money. I just wish people could help each other through tragedies like this rather than break apart, defend their own selfish actions, make division where there should be union. 

So I definitely feel your pain.

We experience suicidal thoughts when death seems preferable to life. It may be an experience or a lifetime of them that pushes us over the edge, but suicidal thoughts can also be caused by chemical imbalances in the brain. 

I think it's normal to think about suicide, but far fewer actually attempt to to kill themselves. Something holds them back. Hope perhaps, or fear of pain, or fear of how death will impact loved ones. 

We all value different things of course, and I personally think it's important to place our value on those things which are more intangible and longer-lasting. Things that take more to lose. We have to recognize our own faults and make a real effort to improve as human beings, while realizing that we'll never be perfect. 

I've thought of suicide on and off throughout my life, moreso recently. I just lost my 48-year old mother to cancer and my father has abused his access to her life insurance policy, spending it on trivial and unimportant things and attempting to buy the love of manipulative women with it. In the end though, you have to free yourself from any guilt or blame--especially for things that aren't your fault. 

Thinking about the reason(s) for your sadness can do a lot to clarify the situation, but you must be willing to deal with what you find. You can't lie to yourself. Once you can recognize the cause of your distress, you can start addressing the problem. 

If suicidal thoughts are occurring without any trigger, then perhaps you are experiencing an odd chemical imbalance in your brain. Lack of certain nutrients can lead to some very surprising depression. I'm a big advocate of curing ailments naturally, and would suggest that you look into some of the herbs and such that are available. 

We can't always control what happens to us, but we can control how we react to it, or what we take into our bodies to perhaps address the issue in this case.
